episode.title: Fail closed when tool-call completeness evidence is reused, ambiguous, missing, or truncated
episode.before: At parent b348fc26674189f758d5941cdab3f78f258b2aa7, the session created an optional recorder solely from startup feature state and did not seed it with initial-history identifiers. Cell completion was derived mainly from recording lifecycle state; reused call IDs or runtime cell IDs, duplicate or mismatched exec/wait input-output associations, missing historical identity evidence, and damaged retained inventories were not comprehensively prevented from receiving or regaining a completeness marker. Prompt-budget truncation could revoke completeness broadly instead of limiting invalidation to outputs belonging to the damaged cell.
episode.after: At 03f014564deef528c25e80fe67ec51871cb6ee51, the recorder indexes bounded call-ID evidence from initial history, tracks call and runtime-cell identities without allowing observations to become fresh again, and withholds completeness when identity freshness cannot be proved. Prompt attachment validates unique outputs and their exec/wait associations, propagates irreversible invalidation across the affected runtime cell, and refuses wait completeness after resume or fork. Budget enforcement preserves per-output omission markers, clears completeness only across damaged cells, and retains unrelated complete outputs. Recording can also be enabled or disabled from live runtime configuration without changing execution-feature dispatch, while legacy configuration reloads preserve the current recorder.
episode.diff: The commit changes 12 Rust files (+1772/-638). It introduces a bounded SeenIds tracker; seeds recorder state from InitialHistory; records wrapper origins and invalidates reused identifiers; validates exec/wait inputs against outputs and runtime cells during prompt attachment; preserves incomplete state through retries and compaction; makes truncation and omission accounting local to each output while propagating damage only within its cell; refreshes recorder enablement separately from execution features; updates construction call sites; and adds unit and integration regressions for reused IDs, wrapper mismatches, paginated or missing history, forked/resumed waits, compaction, runtime recording changes, and metadata budgeting.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 03f014564deef528c25e80fe67ec51871cb6ee51 is titled “Harden Code Mode tool-call completeness tracking (#44472)” and identifies reused IDs, ambiguous exec/wait associations, missing history, cell-local truncation, and runtime recording refresh as the change scope.

The parent recorder stored state as Option<Arc<Mutex<...>>> initialized only from feature enablement; the new recorder always retains a shared optional state, accepts InitialHistory, seeds seen identifiers, and records whether wait completion can be proved for the history type.

SeenIds uses a fixed-size bitset with four probes, separate call-ID and runtime-cell namespaces, maximum ID/history bounds, and bits that are never cleared; collisions or oversized/unindexed history can withhold freshness but cannot make a previously observed identifier fresh.
Session creation now passes initial_history to ExecutedToolCalls::new, connecting recorder identity decisions to new, cleared, resumed, forked, and compacted session history.

Direct wrapper calls, direct tool calls, cell starts, and cell registrations observe identifiers and invalidate the originating call or runtime cell on reuse; cell completion starts as incomplete when origin freshness, runtime-cell freshness, or complete history indexing cannot be proved.
evidence_units.source: 03f014564deef528c25e80fe67ec51871cb6ee51:codex-rs/core/src/tools/executed_tool_calls.rs; invalidate_origin, observe_cell_origin, invalidate_cell, record_call, register_cell, start_cell

evidence_units.claim: Prompt attachment counts duplicate outputs, indexes unique inputs, verifies that an exec or wait input precedes and matches its output and runtime cell, rejects direct/nested collisions, and ANDs retained completeness with intact inventory and association evidence so a retry cannot restore invalidated completeness.
Wait completion is withheld for resumed or forked history because runtime cell handles can restart, while custom exec outputs can still be certified from locally observed evidence.
evidence_units.source: 03f014564deef528c25e80fe67ec51871cb6ee51:codex-rs/core/src/tools/executed_tool_calls.rs and request_metadata.rs; can_prove_wait_completion initialization and completion predicate

evidence_units.claim: Recorder tests cover finished lossless recording, waits, paginated history with known-ID rejection, forked waits, wrapper mismatch, reused origins, direct-ID collision, compaction after truncation, missing history budget, and retained completeness behavior.

Prompt-budget enforcement now records damaged cell IDs, replaces only an over-budget output's calls with its own bounded omission marker, clears completeness across outputs sharing that damaged cell, and leaves unrelated cells' completion claims intact.

Protocol tests assert that truncating one cell clears completion for that cell while preserving an unrelated cell, that omission counts remain local and cumulative on rebounding, and that completeness metadata remains host-only and fail-closed.

End-to-end Code Mode regressions exercise compaction identity retention, resumed waits with reused runtime cells, live recording enablement, and preservation of an unrelated complete call during truncation.

Runtime configuration refresh updates recorder enablement from the incoming feature snapshot without changing execution-feature dispatch; legacy configuration reload explicitly skips recorder refresh to preserve the live recorder.

A unit test verifies that recorder enablement follows runtime configuration without changing execution features, that enabling after unknown history does not claim completeness, and that disabling stops result-metadata recording.
Recorder constructor call sites in session tests and the MCP handler test were updated to supply an explicit InitialHistory, demonstrating that history is now a required contract input.

candidate_atomics.name: track-bounded-identity-evidence
candidate_atomics.description: Track historical and runtime identifiers with bounded, monotonic evidence so reused or unindexable identities cannot support a fresh completeness proof.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent reused, oversized, or insufficiently indexed identifiers from falsely establishing that a structured tool-call inventory is complete.
semantic_action.pre_state: Completeness tracking has call and runtime-cell identifiers but lacks bounded historical freshness evidence or can treat reused identifiers as a new execution.
semantic_action.post_state: Every relevant identifier is observed in a bounded monotonic tracker; reuse, collisions, oversized IDs, or incomplete history indexing withhold freshness and force affected records incomplete.
semantic_action.validation: Unit tests reject known IDs from history, reused origins, direct-ID collisions, and forked waits while allowing genuinely fresh origins.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-wrapper-output-associations
candidate_atomics.description: Validate unique exec/wait input-output associations and retained inventories before attaching or restoring a completeness marker.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure a completion claim describes the exact, uniquely associated execution whose full recorded inventory is still present.
semantic_action.pre_state: Recorded calls, outputs, retry snapshots, or wait results may have duplicate IDs, mismatched wrappers, missing inputs, collisions, or previously damaged inventories.
semantic_action.post_state: Completeness is attached only when the output is unique, any present input precedes and semantically matches it, the retained inventory is intact, and the session can prove the relevant runtime identity; invalidation persists across retries and the affected cell.
semantic_action.validation: Recorder and end-to-end tests exercise wrapper mismatch, duplicate/reused identifiers, compaction, forked/resumed waits, and prove that later waits or retries do not restore an invalid claim.

candidate_atomics.name: localize-budget-damage-by-cell
candidate_atomics.description: Bound structured metadata per output and revoke completeness only for the execution cell whose evidence was truncated or removed.

semantic_action.intent: Fit recorded tool-call evidence within the metadata budget without letting damaged evidence certify completeness or unnecessarily invalidating unrelated executions.
semantic_action.pre_state: Serialized tool-call metadata exceeds its prompt budget, and calls or marker-only outputs may belong to multiple independent execution cells.
semantic_action.post_state: Each over-budget output retains a local bounded omission marker when possible; completeness is cleared across that output's damaged cell, while unrelated cells and their complete inventories remain unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Protocol tests verify local omission counts and cell-wide invalidation, and an end-to-end test verifies that an unrelated complete call survives another cell's truncation.

candidate_atomics.name: refresh-recorder-without-changing-execution
candidate_atomics.description: Apply live recording rollout changes independently from execution-feature dispatch and preserve the live recorder during legacy reloads.

semantic_action.intent: Allow telemetry recording enablement to follow runtime configuration without silently enabling or disabling tool execution and without certifying history that was never observed.
semantic_action.pre_state: Recorder allocation is fixed at session construction, while runtime rollout configuration may change and legacy snapshots may contain stale execution-feature values.
semantic_action.post_state: Normal runtime refresh can create or remove recorder state independently of execution features; a newly enabled recorder marks prior history unobserved, and legacy reload paths leave the live recorder unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: The runtime-refresh unit test checks independent enablement, absence of completeness after unknown history, disabled recording behavior, and unchanged execution features.

candidate_workflows.name: establish-fail-closed-tool-call-completeness
candidate_workflows.description: Build and maintain a trustworthy completeness claim by establishing bounded identity provenance, validating exact wrapper/output relationships, and localizing any evidence loss caused by metadata budgeting.

workflow_graph.goal: Emit a structured tool-call completeness marker only when the host can prove that the exact execution's full call inventory remains uniquely associated and lossless.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A session records nested or direct tool calls across exec/wait outputs, retries, compaction, resume or fork boundaries, under a bounded prompt-metadata budget.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Fresh identities and exact associations may carry completeness; reused, ambiguous, historically unknown, mismatched, or truncated evidence remains incomplete, and damage to one cell does not revoke unrelated valid cells.

candidate_workflows.name: apply-live-recorder-rollout-safely
candidate_workflows.description: Refresh recording state from live configuration while keeping execution behavior and legacy reload semantics independent.

workflow_graph.goal: Change whether structured tool-call evidence is recorded at runtime without changing which tools can execute or making unsupported claims about earlier history.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A live session receives a new runtime feature snapshot or reloads a legacy configuration snapshot.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Live rollout refreshes update only recorder availability, newly started recording treats earlier history as unknown, and legacy reloads preserve the existing live recorder.
unresolved_or_deferred: This configuration workflow is independently testable but supports the broader completeness contract only when recording is enabled.
